Practical gains at small budgets, and a tokenizer gap that remains
Growing a looped generator in depth during training shows no measurable loss of quality at equal or lower
compute (applied layers): 24.52 (12 → 16) and 24.17 (12 → 16 → 20) vs 25.10 for 16 layers from scratch; ties, not an
improvement (section 5). Two tokenizer tests failed; the 1.39× gap and all v0.1 conclusions stand. “Official” = the
Next-Concept Models generate text through a hierarchy of discrete codes. I train both the tokenizer and
generator on one RTX 3080 Ti (12 GB), using TinyStories and budgets far below the original paper. Data-based
codebook initialisation lowers generative perplexity by 48% in the tested tokenizer comparison. A retuned
generator recipe lowers it by 56% on the official tokenizer, with most of the gain coming from the learning rate.
Longer tokenizer training helps, but a 1.39× gap to the official tokenizer remains. The study reports reproducible
runs, unsuccessful interventions and limits on causal interpretation.

What the comparison controls, what it does not, and where the idea comes from.
The 4.7% rule for two-seed means at 409,600 stories was written before the seed-43 runs, but after the seed-42
results were known. The comparison of grown 12 to 16 to 20 with the 12-layer generator was added at that point,
when seed 42 had already shown −5.2%; with both seeds it is −6.6%, beyond the threshold but with more compute
(16 applied layers on average against 12). Against the record table: #3 and #4 against #1 (−5.3% and −6.6%) exceed
4.7%, both with more compute (14 and 16 against 12).
Training time summed over the logged intervals (stories / measured throughput), excluding pauses and repeated steps. * Resumed
after an unplanned shutdown (the grown run before its switch step); the 16-from-scratch seed-43 run also shared the CPU with a
data-preprocessing job. Grown 12 → 16 took 3–13% less time than 16 from scratch in these runs.
• Initialisation. Upstream scales the initial weights of residual projections by the number of layers, and looped models are built
with the full number of applied layers (16 or 20) even while 12 are active. A grown model before its switch is not identical to
the standard 12-layer model, and grown 12 → 16 → 20 differs in initialisation from 16 from scratch. The clean comparison is
grown 12 → 16 against 16 from scratch: identical initial weights, same seed, system and code.
• System. The 12-layer baselines were trained and evaluated on Windows 10 (v0.1); all looped runs on Ubuntu.
• Independence. Seeds change initialisation and corruption and dropout noise; the data order is the same in every run, and
both grown runs of a seed share one from-scratch reference. The four comparisons are not independent; two seeds probably
• Thresholds. 4.7% and 6.7% come from seed noise of standard generators at 51,200 stories and are reused at 409,600.
Growing a looped transformer by increasing the number of loops during training is prior work: looping “provides a
mechanism for model growth, by increasing the number of loops during training” [10]; UpLoop grows depth by copying
learned layers and then loops a shared middle block [11]. Depth growth by stacking goes back to [6, 7]; looped,
shared-weight transformers to [8]; looping has also been applied to masked diffusion language models [12]. The design
here was inspired by Dory1.0-4B [9]. The contribution of this section is only the measurement on an NCM generator

6 Level 0: an observation, not a cause
The coarsest code plays different roles in reconstruction and in the generator’s conditioning.
Decoded tokens changed by an L0 swap
Generator loss rise after an L0 swap
The official decoder is nearly insensitive to swapping level 0, yet the generator relies on that code: its loss rises
when level 0 comes from a different story. In several tokenizers trained here, the decoder is more sensitive. This
makes the role of level 0 a useful open question, not a demonstrated explanation of the PPL gap.
The tokenizer trained at batch 4,096 also has an almost inert level 0: only 0.05% of decoded tokens change when
it is swapped. Its Gen. PPL is still 100.36. An inert level 0 alone is therefore insufficient to reproduce the official
